correctness.rationale: The gradient of the restricted determinant comprises all allowed cofactors. A corank-one adjugate is rank one, so gradient-vanishing forces its support rectangle to be a singleton forbidden matching cell, equivalently one full zero row/column. Rank<=n-2 is an irreducible codimension-four linear section by an integral bilinear-quadric factorization U V^T, with smooth rank-(n-2) witnesses from allowed partial permutations. The k remaining row/column zero linear strata are distinct and generically corank-one. All singular components have codimension >=3 inside the hypersurface, forcing squarefree irreducible F and normality by S2/R1. Schur complements give nondegenerate transverse quadratic forms. The codimension and degree formulas follow from dimension and Porteous. Exactly 65668 cofactor/rank finite tests and nine corank-two Jacobian rank witnesses passed, corroborative only. No unproved infinite step is delegated to computation.

value.rationale: Sparse determinants are a natural, extensively studied algebraic-geometric class, and rank-one adjugate degenerations under coordinate restrictions are a motivated gap beyond generic determinantal loci. The theorem provides a natural complete infinite classification with exactly k+1 irreducible singular components, all component codimensions, an exact nontrivial determinantal degree, normality, and two structurally different generic transverse quadratic cones. These distinguish the extra singularities introduced by each zero cell and are not a numerical one-off or trivial restatement of known primality results.
